start.title: The Master's Charge
start.text:
Abraham is old. He places your hand under his thigh.
"Swear by the Lord — do not take a wife for Isaac from the Canaanites."

choices.text: Swear and accept the journey to his homeland
choices.feedback: You give your word. The journey begins in your heart.

choices.text: Refuse — the road is too long for an old servant
choices.feedback: Abraham's eyes do not waver. The promise is heavier than the road.

choices.text: Suggest a Canaanite girl from a wealthy house
choices.feedback: "No," he says. "Not from this land. The Lord swore to my fathers."

refuse_consequence.title: Faith Over Fear
refuse_consequence.text:
Abraham only smiles. "The Lord who took me from my father's house
will send His angel before you."

choices.text: Yield, and swear the oath
choices.feedback: You bow low. "I will go."

canaan_consequence.title: Not From This Land
canaan_consequence.text:
"My son must not return there. But you are free of the oath
if the woman will not follow."

choices.text: Accept and swear properly
choices.feedback: You place your hand again, and swear by the Lord.

the_oath.title: Ten Camels Loaded
the_oath.text:
You take ten camels and the best of your master's goods.
The road to Mesopotamia is long. Aram-Naharaim waits.

choices.text: Set out at once with quiet trust
choices.feedback: You turn the caravan north. The desert opens before you.

choices.text: Delay — gather more men and weapons first
choices.feedback: You linger over preparations. But faith does not wait on iron.

delay_consequence.title: The Lord Is Your Guard
delay_consequence.text:
Abraham's words return to you: "His angel will go before you."
No blade you carry will weigh more than that promise.

choices.text: Set out in faith, with what you have
choices.feedback: You leave at first light. The camels' bells ring across the dunes.

the_well.title: The Well of Nahor
the_well.text:
Evening. You arrive at a stone well outside the city of Nahor.
The time when the women come out to draw water.

choices.text: Make the camels kneel and pray for a sign
choices.feedback: You bow your head beside the kneeling beasts. "O Lord, God of my master Abraham…"

choices.text: Walk into the city and ask for Nahor's house
choices.feedback: Strangers are wary. No one knows you. You return to the well, weary.

choices.text: Pick the most beautiful girl you see
choices.feedback: Beauty is not the sign. Your master sent you for kindness, not a face.

city_consequence.title: Back to the Well
city_consequence.text:
The city is closed to a stranger. The well is where God answers.
You kneel beside the camels.

choices.text: Pray for a sign instead
choices.feedback: "Lord, give me success today," you whisper.

beauty_consequence.title: Not What You See
beauty_consequence.text:
Your master did not send you for the eyes of men.
He sent you for the heart God will choose.

choices.text: Bow your head and ask for the true sign
choices.feedback: You forget the faces and pray instead.

the_prayer.title: The Sign You Ask
the_prayer.text: What sign will you set before the Lord?

choices.text: "She who offers to water my camels — let her be the one"
choices.feedback: The words are barely out of your mouth when a girl appears with a jar on her shoulder.

choices.text: "Send me a sign of fire from heaven"
choices.feedback: The sky stays still. God answers in kindness, not in flame.

choices.text: "The first one to greet me — let her be the one"
choices.feedback: A greeting costs nothing. Your master needs a heart that gives.

fire_consequence.title: Quiet Heaven
fire_consequence.text:
The heavens do not roar. They wait.
The sign of God's choice will be a small kindness, not a wonder.

choices.text: Ask instead for the one who waters the camels
choices.feedback: You change your prayer — and a girl steps from the city gate.

greeting_consequence.title: More Than Words
greeting_consequence.text:
Words are easy. Service is the heart God reads.
Ask for the sign that costs something.

choices.text: Pray for the one who will water the camels
choices.feedback: You change the prayer — and look up.

rebekah_arrives.title: A Girl at the Well
rebekah_arrives.text:
She is young, careful, lovely.
She fills her jar and turns to leave.

choices.text: Run to her: "Please give me a little water from your jar"
choices.feedback: Your voice is humble. She stops and turns.

choices.text: Order her to water your camels at once
choices.feedback: Her face hardens. She walks away without a word.

command_consequence.title: Pride Drives Her Away
command_consequence.text:
She is gone. The camels are still thirsty.
You must wait — and ask the next one with humility.

choices.text: Wait, and ask the next girl gently
choices.feedback: She returns again, having forgotten her sandal. You speak softly this time.

rebekah_pov_request.title: A Stranger's Voice
rebekah_pov_request.text:
You are Rebekah, daughter of Bethuel.
A dusty old man at the well asks for a sip of water.

choices.text: "Drink, my lord" — and offer to draw for his camels too
choices.feedback: You lower the jar to his hands. "I will draw for your camels also, until they have done."

choices.text: Give him only a sip and hurry home
choices.feedback: Your jar is heavy. But the camels watch you with tired, dust-rimmed eyes.

choices.text: Refuse — your father warned you about strangers
choices.feedback: He has not asked for much. A sip of water is no danger.

stingy_consequence.title: The Camels' Eyes
stingy_consequence.text:
Ten camels. Days in the desert. Their thirst is enormous.
Your mother taught you better than this.

choices.text: Turn back and offer to water them all
choices.feedback: You return to the trough. "I will draw for your camels also."

refuse_water_consequence.title: A Sip Is No Sin
refuse_water_consequence.text:
He is old and bent and dusty. The well is the gathering place.
Hospitality is the law of your people.

choices.text: Offer him drink — and the camels too
choices.feedback: You lift the jar. "Drink, my lord."

watering_camels.title: Until They Have Done
watering_camels.text:
You run between well and trough until your arms ache.
Ten camels drink their fill. The old man watches you in silence.

choices.text: Finish the work fully, then ask if he needs more
choices.feedback: You set the empty jar down. He has not moved his eyes from you.

choices.text: Stop halfway — surely that is enough
choices.feedback: The camels still murmur with thirst. The work is not done.

halfway_consequence.title: Until the Last One Drinks
halfway_consequence.text:
The Lord watches the work that is finished, not begun.
The camels are still pressing close to the trough.

choices.text: Return to the well and finish
choices.feedback: You draw and pour until every beast turns away satisfied.

the_gifts.title: Gold in His Hand
the_gifts.text:
The old servant takes a heavy gold ring and two bracelets.
"Tell me — whose daughter are you? Is there room in your father's house?"

choices.text: "I am Bethuel's daughter — son of Milcah and Nahor"
choices.feedback: His face changes. He bows his head to the ground at once.

choices.text: Hide your name — he might be a thief
choices.feedback: His kind eyes do not look like a thief's. The truth would have cost you nothing.

choices.text: Take the gold and run home without answering
choices.feedback: You clutch the gold to your chest. But the man's voice follows you, gentle, unhurried.

hide_consequence.title: The Lord's Hand Is Plain
hide_consequence.text:
The man's tears say what no thief could fake.
"Blessed be the Lord, the God of my master Abraham," he murmurs.

choices.text: Tell him your true name
choices.feedback: "I am Rebekah, daughter of Bethuel, son of Milcah."

run_consequence.title: He Has Not Wronged You
run_consequence.text:
He is old, alone, and weeping with joy beside the well.
This is no robber. The Lord is in this meeting.

choices.text: Return and tell him your name
choices.feedback: You walk back. "I am Rebekah, daughter of Bethuel."

the_blessing_well.title: Blessed Be the Lord
the_blessing_well.text:
He bows his head to the ground, weeping.
"Blessed be the Lord, who has led me to the house of my master's brothers."

choices.text: Run home and tell your mother's house everything
choices.feedback: You run, the gold catching the last sun. The house must hear of this.

choices.text: Say nothing — keep the gold for yourself
choices.feedback: The Lord's hand cannot be hidden in a pocket. Your mother sees the gold at once.

secret_consequence.title: The Gold Speaks for You
secret_consequence.text:
The bracelets shine on your wrist. Your mother gasps.
She asks for the whole story.

choices.text: Tell her everything truthfully
choices.feedback: Your brother Laban listens with widening eyes — and runs out toward the well.

laban_meets.title: Laban Brings Him In
laban_meets.text:
Your brother Laban runs to the well and brings the man home.
The camels are unloaded. Water is brought for his feet.

choices.text: Set bread and wine before him at once
choices.feedback: Food is laid on the low table. He raises his hand: "I will not eat until I have told my errand."

choices.text: Demand to know his business first
choices.feedback: His face stiffens. A guest is honored before he is questioned.

demand_consequence.title: First the Welcome
demand_consequence.text:
Your father Bethuel shakes his head gently.
"Bread first. Then his words."

choices.text: Set the table and listen properly
choices.feedback: You bring the bread. The lamp is lit. He begins to speak.

the_errand_told.title: I Am Abraham's Servant
the_errand_told.text:
He tells everything — the oath, the journey, the prayer at the well,
your kindness, the sign of the Lord. The room is silent.

choices.text: Bethuel and Laban speak: "This thing is from the Lord"
choices.feedback: "We cannot speak to you bad or good. Take her, and let her be your master's son's wife."

choices.text: Refuse — the journey is too far, and he is a stranger
choices.feedback: The servant lifts his hands. "Hinder me not — the Lord has prospered my way."

stranger_consequence.title: The Lord Has Prospered His Way
stranger_consequence.text:
Every word he has spoken bears the mark of God's hand.
Who can stand against what the Lord has chosen?

choices.text: Bow to the will of the Lord
choices.feedback: Your father lifts his eyes. "Let it be as the Lord has said."

rebekahs_choice.title: Will You Go With This Man?
rebekahs_choice.text:
In the morning the servant says: "Send me away to my master."
Your family asks: "Let her stay with us a few days — at least ten."
Then they turn to you. "Will you go with this man?"

choices.text: "I will go."
choices.feedback: Two words. Quiet, certain. The whole house falls still.

choices.text: "Let me wait ten days at least"
choices.feedback: The servant's face is pleading. The Lord's hand has been on this from the first hour.

choices.text: "I will not leave my mother's house"
choices.feedback: Your mother lowers her eyes. The God who called Abraham is calling you now.

wait_consequence.title: The Lord Has Already Spoken
wait_consequence.text:
The sign was given. The gold was given. The way is opened.
What is ten days against the call of God?

choices.text: Change your answer — "I will go."
choices.feedback: You straighten. "I will go." Your nurse begins quietly to pack.

stay_consequence.title: A Larger House Waits
stay_consequence.text:
Your mother takes your hand. "Daughter, the Lord has chosen.
Go where He sends. Our blessing goes with you."

choices.text: Answer at last: "I will go."
choices.feedback: You let her hand go. "I will go."

the_blessing_send.title: Mother of Thousands
the_blessing_send.text:
Your family blesses you at the door:
"Be the mother of thousands of millions.
May your offspring possess the gates of those who hate them."

choices.text: Mount the camel and ride out with the servant
choices.feedback: Your nurse Deborah climbs up beside you. The caravan turns south toward Canaan.

the_road_home.title: South Toward Canaan
the_road_home.text:
The desert stretches for many days. The servant rides ahead, watchful and quiet.
You feel the Lord's hand on every mile.

choices.text: Trust the journey and pray as you ride
choices.feedback: The wind moves the veil at your face. The sky deepens to evening.

choices.text: Beg the servant to turn the caravan back
choices.feedback: He shakes his head, kindly. "The Lord goes before us, my lady."

turn_back_consequence.title: Forward Is the Way
turn_back_consequence.text:
The Lord has not led you this far to send you back.
The land of promise lies ahead, just over the hills.

choices.text: Settle into the saddle and ride on
choices.feedback: You pull the veil closer. The caravan keeps moving.

isaac_in_field.title: A Man in the Field
isaac_in_field.text:
At evening you see the hills of the Negev.
A man is walking alone in the field, in the time of meditation.

choices.text: Ask the servant: "Who is this man?"
choices.feedback: "It is my master," he says. You take your veil and cover your face.

choices.text: Ride past — he is none of your business
choices.feedback: The servant gently raises his hand: "My lady — that is the man."

ride_past_consequence.title: That Is the Man
ride_past_consequence.text:
Your heart catches in your chest.
You slip down from the camel and take the veil to your face.

choices.text: Walk forward to meet him
choices.feedback: Across the field, Isaac stops. He has been waiting longer than you know.

the_meeting.title: Isaac and Rebekah
the_meeting.text:
The servant tells Isaac everything that has happened.
Isaac brings you into his mother Sarah's tent.

choices.text: Stand with him beneath the open sky
choices.feedback: He takes your hand. The wind is soft over the field of evening.

the_comfort.title: And He Loved Her
the_comfort.text:
Isaac took Rebekah, and she became his wife.
And he loved her — and was comforted after his mother's death.
The promise to Abraham walks on, into another generation.

choices.text: Step into the story God has written
choices.feedback: The lamp glows in Sarah's tent. The covenant continues.
